transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, mostly I'm here because I just don't sleep right anymore. I go to bed and... I just lie there a long time. Then, when I finally do drop off, I end up waking up from bad dreams, or even just little noises in the house. And once I'm awake, I just can't seem to settle back down to get any real rest.
Do you feel anxious or stressed when you're lying in bed trying to fall asleep?

Not really, no. I wouldn't say I feel nervous or stressed out or anything like that. I just... I just lie there awake. It's more like I'm just staring at the ceiling waiting to get tired, but it takes a good long while.
Has there been anything significant happening in your life that you think might be affecting your sleep?

Well... the only thing I can really point to is an accident I had. I fell off a ladder. This whole trouble with sleeping, it's been going on ever since that ladder accident... which was about a year and seven months ago now.
Do you feel tired or fatigued during the day?

No, not really. You'd think I would be, since I'm not getting much sleep, but... I don't feel all that tired when the sun's up. I'm retired, so I just take it easy mostly, and I get through the day just fine.
Do you have dreams or nightmares about the ladder accident?

No, I don't really have dreams or nightmares about it. But... sometimes when I'm awake, it comes back to me. If I hear metal scraping, or even just see a ladder leaning up against a house in somebody's yard... the whole thing just jumps right back into my head. It's like I'm right back under there again, waiting for somebody to come help me.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain activities or places because they remind you of the ladder accident?

Well, yeah, I guess I do. I just... I keep finding reasons not to go work around the garage anymore. Especially over near the tools, or that spot where I used to keep the ladder. I just stay away from it. And I haven't been going down to the senior center much either. I just find excuses not to do those things now.
Has avoiding the garage or the senior center caused any problems for you in your daily life or relationships?

Well, I can still get through my basic daily routine alright. But, you know, since I've been avoiding the garage and certain parts of the yard, my wife has had to take over a lot of the chores I used to handle. And... well, since I stopped going to the senior center, I don't really see my bridge friends much anymore either. I guess you could say my days have just gotten a lot smaller.
{"intent": "determine the presence of hyperarousal", "question": "Do you often feel "on edge" or easily startled?"}

Yeah, I do. If... well, if a door bangs shut loud, or if somebody just comes up behind me, I jump real hard. And then my chest just starts thumping. It keeps pounding for a good while, too, even after I turn around and see that it's nothing to worry about.
How often do you think about going back to the senior center or working in the garage, but then decide not to?

Well, I'm not really sure. I don't keep track or anything. I guess... I don't really sit and debate it in my head all that much. When it comes time to do something out in the garage or head down to the center, I just sort of put it out of my mind and stay put. I haven't really noticed how often it happens, to be honest.
Do you ever feel like you're missing out on things you want to do because you're avoiding certain places or activities?

I don't know that I'd say that. I mean... I haven't really thought about it like that. I guess I don't sit around feeling like I'm missing out on much. I just stay in the house and keep to myself mostly, and... well, it just is what it is. I don't really get upset about missing the center or anything like that.
Do you avoid talking or thinking about the ladder accident?

No, not really. I mean... I don't go out of my way to bring it up, but if somebody asks me about it, I'll tell 'em what happened. I don't try to block it out of my head or anything like that. I think about it sometimes, sure, but I wouldn't say I avoid it.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving the ladder accident when you're awake, like it's happening all over again?

Well, yeah, I guess I do sometimes. Like... if I hear metal scraping against something, or if I'm just driving by and see a ladder leaning up against a house in somebody's yard. It just sort of... jumps right back into my head. It feels like I'm right back under there again, just pinned down and waiting for somebody to come help me. It's real clear when that happens.
Do you try to push thoughts of the ladder accident out of your mind when they come up?

No, not really. Like I was saying a minute ago, I don't try to block it out. If it pops in my head, well... it's just there. I don't fight it or try to force it away. I just sort of let it be until I end up thinking about something else.
Do you ever try to avoid thinking about the ladder accident?
No, like I just mentioned a second ago, I really don't. I don't try to avoid it. If it comes up in my head, I just let it be.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, when you're remembering the ladder accident?
No, I can't say I do. When I remember it, I'm just... well, I'm just me, right in my own shoes. I don't ever feel like I'm floating around or watching myself from the outside or anything like that.
How much of your daily life would you say is affected by avoiding things that remind you of the ladder accident?

Well, I still manage my basic routines, getting up and dressed and all that. But... I guess it affects a fair bit. I've stopped going down to the senior center altogether. And around the house, I just avoid enough things that my wife has to handle a lot of the chores I used to take care of. I don't really visit with my bridge friends much anymore, either. So... my days have just gotten a lot smaller, I suppose.
Would you say that avoiding reminders of the ladder accident is something you do almost every day?

Yeah, I suppose it is pretty much every day. I just... well, I keep finding reasons not to go to the senior center, like I said. And here at home, I stay out of the garage. I make sure I don't go near the tools, or, you know, especially that spot where I used to keep that ladder. I just stay away from it.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms related to the ladder accident?
Well, it's been going on since the accident happened. That was... let's see, about a year and seven months ago now.
